prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which established the basis of incretin-based therapy

statement.case_for: After reading all six first-round statements and the chair's questions, I keep a single-achievement prize for B040 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific chain is complete and independently confirmed: proglucagon processing, GLP-1(7-36) as the active glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide, its actions on islets, gut and appetite circuits, and the large outcome trials showing glycaemic, cardiovascular and renal benefit. On the chair's question about a second part, I do not think one is needed. A second part would force each part to share the three-person limit, which would either shrink the GLP-1 credit or leave a thinly credited second achievement. The fact that all six of us arrived at the same set does not carry the case. What carries it is that the physiological discovery is the object that is mature, well defined and decisive, and the drugs rest on it. The citation should say plainly that Knudsen and the Habener group are not named because the prize is framed around the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form, not because their work was unimportant.
statement.case_against: The attribution risk is unchanged and is the real weakness. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide form is credited but contested, and I cannot adjudicate it from the supplied evidence. Habener-group work lies outside the three names. Excluding Knudsen is a framing choice that a reader of the prize could find too narrow, and it would look worse if the committee later treats analogue design as the decisive step. Durability and long-term safety of the weight effects are still being characterised. There is also the risk that a consensus choice crowds out candidates of equal mechanistic originality, in particular the unfolded protein response, whose credit is cleaner than GLP-1's.

responses.point: The chair said CAR-T is his best second candidate but qualified the Rosenberg inclusion, because adoptive cell transfer and TIL work are a distinct line from engineered CARs and Eshhar's founding chimeric-receptor concept is not in the supplied credit.
responses.response: I accept the chair's correction. In round 1 I proposed June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, and I now think a CAR-specific citation is cleaner with June and Sadelain. Rosenberg's third slot does not close the Eshhar gap, and it blurs what the prize is for. This changes my alternative for B034 but not my preferred configuration. I would still put B034 behind B040 because of the solid-tumour limits, toxicity and secondary-malignancy signals that you and Perlmann cite, although I find those a reason for a later year rather than against the science.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (B039) as the strongest basic-science fallback, with a clean Mori and Walter credit, and treats B025 as the next fallback.
responses.response: You have moved me part of the way. The Mori and Walter credit is the cleanest on the shortlist, and I now name B039 as one of my two alternatives instead of B008. I still do not put it above B040, because the demonstrated change in patients is indirect, and I note that the PERK and ATF6 arms are outside the credited names, so a citation would need to be limited to the IRE1, HAC1 and XBP1 pathway. I agree with you that a separate part for analogue development would dilute B040. I do not agree that a clean credit by itself settles ranking, but it is a real advantage when attribution is the weak point of the lead candidate.

responses.point: Linnarsson regards the unfolded protein response as a strong later candidate rather than a competitor this year and accepts B040 with the exact trio, while saying he would revisit Knudsen if the committee judged drug design decisive.
responses.response: I agree with your timing view on B039 and with your conditional about Knudsen. If the committee decides the drug design is decisive, I think the right change is to replace Mojsov or Holst only after hearing the primary-literature argument, and I do not have that evidence. On optogenetics, where I disclosed that it is a tool in my own field, I now think it is a weaker alternative than B039 or B034. Six credited names against three places leave out Boyden, Bamberg or Miesenböck, and, as you say, the molecular discovery and the neuronal demonstration are different achievements.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius holds that CAR-T is a mature and expanding therapeutic class, and that dropping Rosenberg should not be decided by name count alone.
responses.response: I accept that the adoptive transfer and first gene-engineered T-cell trials are a real antecedent, and that name count should not decide it. But I would settle it by the claim in the citation. A citation to genetically engineered receptors is June and Sadelain, and a broader cell-therapy citation would need a different configuration than the three-person limit allows next to B040. I agree with your point that remission durability and the move into autoimmune disease make B034 a serious alternative, and I keep it as my first alternative for that reason.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority on the active peptide form, relative to the Habener group, is strong enough to hold a place; I cannot verify the primary literature and would be willing to revisit if a colleague presents it.
Whether the committee treats analogue design (Knudsen) as decisive; if so, my configuration would change and I do not know which of the three names should yield.
Whether a CAR-T citation can be limited to the engineered-receptor claim given Eshhar's absence from the credited names.
Whether the narrow IRE1, HAC1 and XBP1 framing of B039 is defensible against the PERK and ATF6 contributions.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: no conflict requiring recusal. I co-authored a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann (a committee member) and shared work with Patrik Ernfors; none of them is a credited name on the shortlist. Optogenetics is a tool in my own field, which I note for transparency, and it is no longer among my alternatives. I have no tie to any credited name for B040, B034 or B039.
